prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. One finished landscape 3:2 full-bleed picture-book illustration, one coherent scene and moment, no panels or contact sheet. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
 No named child cast: Kit and Zoe MUST NOT appear. Include unnamed human workers/adults ONLY when explicitly required by this particular scene; otherwise show only the natural subjects. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Transport Through Time; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: A selected factual history followed by contemporary transport comparisons. Historical pictures are reconstructions, not a claim that all countries changed at once. Plain practical clothes only; no flags, religious buildings, political events or cultural costumes. Cart: brown wooden four-wheel wagon, one healthy bay horse and adult driver in plain gray shirt and dark trousers. Steam train: black early passenger steam locomotive with red wheels and two brown wooden coaches. Early motor car: dark-green open four-wheel gasoline car with adult driver. Early aircraft: plain cream single-propeller biplane. Modern train: white electric passenger train with blue band and overhead wire. Jet: white twin-engine passenger jet with teal tail. No named cast or brand logos.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): Horse-drawn brown wagon; Early black steam train; Early dark-green motor car; Cream early propeller biplane; Modern white-blue electric train; Modern white-teal passenger jet
 Input references lock identity, prop design and location; compose a NEW image for the exact scene, never reproduce the reference-board layout. The reference and overall prop list may contain finished objects and later story events: these are DESIGN REFERENCES ONLY, not permission to show them now. Show only the people, objects and development stage required below.
Page 2. Printed prose (NOT text to put in art): A horse could pull a cart full of people or goods. Travelers still needed to feed and rest the horse.
Required illustration: Historical reconstruction: one bay horse rests beside stationary brown wagon on firm level road. Adult driver offers hay from a small bucket at horse’s head; two travelers sit safely in wagon. Tack and traces connect realistically, all four horse legs clear. No contemporary car.
Exact current state: Animal transport depends on a living animal needing care and rest.
Do not add later events, duplicate props or a separate inset. No written title; the app renders live text.
FINAL QUALITY LOCK: Render 1536 by 1024 pixels, clean landscape 3:2. This is the finished page, not a reference sheet. Keep all essential subjects fully framed with 8 percent margin. Use plain ordinary clothes and exactly the subjects specified in this page. Do not transfer extraneous reference animals, poses or props into the picture. No national symbols, logos or written marks. All wheels visibly contact their own road or rails. Train rails are a coherent parallel pair under the wheels. A locomotive has a plausible horizontal boiler, firebox, steam pipe, cylinder, piston and connecting rods only where explicitly requested. No fantasy plumbing, exposed loose hoses, melted wheels or floating mechanisms. Horses have exactly four natural legs; tack is coherent. Aircraft have exactly one fuselage, one tail and matching wings with correct attachment.
COMPOSITION CORRECTION: Preserve all exact content and physical contacts of the generated draft: one feeding adult, one four-legged bay horse in coherent harness, one stationary four-wheel wooden wagon with two seated travelers, bucket and hay. Zoom the entire subject group OUT by 18 percent and recenter so every complete person, horse hoof, bucket, wagon edge and wheel stays within x150..1386 and y120..900 of the 1536x1024 canvas. Extend the same ordinary background field/river and road around this smaller group. Do not crop the driver at the left or wagon at the right. No extra people or animals.

visualReview.note: Stationary bay horse has four grounded legs and connected bridle/harness/shafts; gray driver offers hay from a bucket while two ordinary-clothed travelers sit safely in four-wheel wooden wagon. No movement or extra animal. Producer independently inspected the final installed WebP natively; complete final sequence and relevant native diagrams were independently reviewed.
